title: Telling Time to the Hour, Half Hour and Quarter Hour
seo_title: Grade 1 Telling Time Worksheets with Answers (MATATAG Math 1)
standard_text: Read and write time by the hour, half hour, and quarter hour using an analog clock.
meta_desc: Free Grade 1 telling time worksheets for the DepEd MATATAG curriculum: o'clock, half past, quarter past and quarter to on analog clocks, and daily routines. 100 questions with pictures and answers.
key_big: Short hand: hour. Long hand: minutes.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • The short hand is the hour hand. The long hand is the minute hand.
  • When the minute hand points to 12, it is o'clock: 7:00.
  • When it points to 6, it is half past: 7:30. The hour hand is halfway between 7 and 8.
  • Quarter past is :15 (minute hand at 3). Quarter to is :45 (minute hand at 9).

Examples

Example

Minute hand at 3, hour hand just past 9

quarter past 9

Answer: 9:15

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Mixing the handsThe short hand shows the hour.
Half past 4 as 5:30Half past 4 is 4:30.
Quarter past or to?Quarter past: 15 minutes after.

faq.q: What does MATATAG Math 1 ask about time?
faq.a: Read and write time by the hour, half hour, and quarter hour using an analog clock, and solve problems involving time.

faq.q: How many minutes are in an hour?

faq.a: Many clocks at home and school have hands.

items.e: The long hand points to the 12. The short hand points to the 8. It is 8 o’clock. (Not 12 o’clock: the long hand on the 12 only tells us it is o’clock. The short hand tells the hour.)
The long hand points to the 12. The short hand points to the 7. It is 7 o’clock. (Not 12 o’clock: the long hand on the 12 only tells us it is o’clock. The short hand tells the hour.)
The long hand points to the 12. The short hand points to the 3. It is 3 o’clock. (Not 12 o’clock: the long hand on the 12 only tells us it is o’clock. The short hand tells the hour.)
The long hand points to the 12. The short hand points to the 9. It is 9 o’clock. (Not 12 o’clock: the long hand on the 12 only tells us it is o’clock. The short hand tells the hour.)
The long hand points to the 12. The short hand points to the 6. It is 6 o’clock. (Not 12 o’clock: the long hand on the 12 only tells us it is o’clock. The short hand tells the hour.)
The long hand points to the 12. The short hand points to the 7. So clock C shows 7 o’clock. (Clock A has the hands swapped: its short hand is near the 12 and its long hand is on the 7.)
The long hand points to the 12. The short hand points to the 10. It is 10 o’clock. (Not 12 o’clock: the long hand on the 12 only tells us it is o’clock. The short hand tells the hour.)

items.q: At 4 o’clock, where does the long hand point?
items.e: At every o’clock time the long hand points straight up to the 12. The short hand points to the 4.
The long hand points to the 12. The short hand points to the 2. It is 2 o’clock. (Not 12 o’clock: the long hand on the 12 only tells us it is o’clock. The short hand tells the hour.)
The long hand points to the 12. The short hand points to the 2. So clock A shows 2 o’clock. (Clock B has the hands swapped: its long hand is on the 2.)

items.q: At 9 o’clock, where does the short hand point?
items.e: The short hand shows the hour. At 9 o’clock it points right at the 9. The long hand points to the 12.
The long hand points to the 12. The short hand points to the 5. It is 5 o’clock. (Not 12 o’clock: the long hand on the 12 only tells us it is o’clock. The short hand tells the hour.)

items.q: What time is this?
items.e: On a digital clock the number before the colon is the hour: 5. The 00 means 0 minutes past. It is 5 o’clock.
The long hand points to the 12. The short hand points to the 11. It is 11 o’clock. (Not 12 o’clock: the long hand on the 12 only tells us it is o’clock. The short hand tells the hour.)
8 o’clock is 8 hours and 0 minutes. On a digital clock it is 8:00. (Not 8:12: the long hand on the 12 means 0 minutes, not 12 minutes.)

items.q: The short hand points to the 6. The long hand points to the 12. What time is it?
items.e: The short hand tells the hour: 6. The long hand on the 12 means o’clock. It is 6 o’clock. (12 o’clock mixes up the hands.)
The long hand points to the 12. The short hand points to the 4. It is 4 o’clock. (Not 12 o’clock: the long hand on the 12 only tells us it is o’clock. The short hand tells the hour.)
The long hand points to the 12. The short hand points to the 10. So clock D shows 10 o’clock. (Clock B has the hands swapped: its long hand is on the 10.)
The long hand points to the 12. The short hand points to the 1. It is 1 o’clock. (Not 12 o’clock: the long hand on the 12 only tells us it is o’clock. The short hand tells the hour.)

items.q: The long hand goes all the way around once. How long is that?
items.e: When the long hand goes all the way around, the short hand moves from one number to the next. From 3 o’clock to 4 o’clock is 1 hour.
The long hand points to the 6: half way round. The short hand is half way between 2 and 3, so the hour is still 2. It is half past 2. (Not half past 3: the short hand has not reached the 3 yet.)

The long hand points to the 6: half way round. The short hand is half way between 11 and 12, so the hour is still 11. It is half past 11. (Not half past 12: the short hand has not reached the 12 yet.)

The long hand points to the 6: half way round. The short hand is half way between 10 and 11, so the hour is still 10. It is half past 10. (Not half past 11: the short hand has not reached the 11 yet.)
The long hand points to the 6: half way round. The short hand is half way between 3 and 4, so the hour is still 3. It is half past 3. (Not half past 4: the short hand has not reached the 4 yet.)
The long hand points to the 6: half way round. The short hand is half way between 1 and 2, so the hour is still 1. It is half past 1. (Not half past 2: the short hand has not reached the 2 yet.)

items.q: At half past 4, where does the long hand point?
items.e: Half past means the long hand has gone half way round, from the 12 to the 6.
The long hand points to the 6: half way round. The short hand is half way between 4 and 5, so the hour is still 4. It is half past 4. (Not half past 5: the short hand has not reached the 5 yet.)

items.q: At half past 8, where is the short hand?
items.e: In half an hour the short hand moves half way to the next number. At half past 8 it is between 8 and 9.

The long hand points to the 6: half way round. The short hand is half way between 2 and 3, so the hour is still 2. So clock B shows half past 2. (Clock A shows half past 3: its short hand is past the 3. Clock C has the hands swapped.)
The long hand points to the 6: half way round. The short hand is half way between 9 and 10, so the hour is still 9. It is half past 9. (Not half past 10: the short hand has not reached the 10 yet.)

items.q: What time is this?
items.e: The hour is 3 and the minutes are 30. 30 minutes is half an hour. It is half past 3. (Not half past 4: it is not 4 o’clock yet.)
Half past 10 is 30 minutes after 10 o’clock. On a digital clock it is 10:30. (Not 10:06: the long hand on the 6 means 30 minutes.)
The long hand points to the 6: half way round. The short hand is half way between 7 and 8, so the hour is still 7. It is half past 7. (Not half past 8: the short hand has not reached the 8 yet.)

items.q: How many minutes are in half an hour?
items.e: 1 hour is 60 minutes. Half of 60 is 30.

items.q: The long hand moves from the 12 to the 6. How long is that?
items.e: The long hand goes half way around the clock. That is half an hour (30 minutes).
The long hand points to the 6: half way round. The short hand is half way between 8 and 9, so the hour is still 8. It is half past 8. (Not half past 9: the short hand has not reached the 9 yet.)

The long hand points to the 6: half way round. The short hand is half way between 9 and 10, so the hour is still 9. So clock D shows half past 9. (Clock A shows half past 10. Clock C has the hands swapped.)

items.q: Half past 11 is half an hour after which time?
items.e: Half past 11 is 30 minutes after 11 o’clock. It comes before 12 o’clock.
The long hand points to the 6: half way round. The short hand is half way between 12 and 1, so the hour is still 12. It is half past 12. (Not half past 1: the short hand has not reached the 1 yet.)

items.q: Half past 7 is how many minutes after 7 o’clock?
items.e: Half an hour is 30 minutes. (6 is the number the long hand points to, not the minutes.)
The long hand points to the 3: a quarter of the way round. The short hand is just past the 11. It is quarter past 11. (Quarter to is when the long hand is on the 9.)

The long hand points to the 9: a quarter of an hour before the 12. The short hand is nearly at the 6, but not there yet. It is quarter to 6. (Not quarter to 5: the short hand has passed the 5, so the next hour is 6.)
The long hand points to the 3: a quarter of the way round. The short hand is just past the 10. It is quarter past 10. (Quarter to is when the long hand is on the 9.)

The long hand points to the 9: a quarter of an hour before the 12. The short hand is nearly at the 12, but not there yet. It is quarter to 12. (Not quarter to 11: the short hand has passed the 11, so the next hour is 12.)
The long hand points to the 3: a quarter of the way round. The short hand is just past the 2. It is quarter past 2. (Quarter to is when the long hand is on the 9.)

items.q: At quarter past, where does the long hand point?
items.e: Quarter past means the long hand has gone a quarter of the way round, from the 12 to the 3. (The 9 is for quarter to.)

The long hand points to the 9: a quarter of an hour before the 12. The short hand is nearly at the 3, but not there yet. It is quarter to 3. (Not quarter to 2: the short hand has passed the 2, so the next hour is 3.)

items.q: At quarter to, where does the long hand point?
items.e: Quarter to means a quarter of an hour before the 12. The long hand points to the 9. (The 3 is for quarter past.)
The long hand points to the 3: a quarter of the way round. The short hand is just past the 5. It is quarter past 5. (Quarter to is when the long hand is on the 9.)

items.q: Quarter past 5 is how many minutes after 5 o’clock?
items.e: A quarter of an hour is 15 minutes. Count in 5s from the 12 to the 3: 5, 10, 15. (3 is the number, not the minutes.)

The long hand points to the 9: a quarter of an hour before the 12. The short hand is nearly at the 11, but not there yet. It is quarter to 11. (Not quarter to 10: the short hand has passed the 10, so the next hour is 11.)

The long hand points to the 9: a quarter of an hour before the 12. The short hand is nearly at the 4, but not there yet. So clock B shows quarter to 4. (Clock A shows quarter past 4, not quarter to 4. Clock D has the hands swapped.)
The long hand points to the 3: a quarter of the way round. The short hand is just past the 12. It is quarter past 12. (Quarter to is when the long hand is on the 9.)

items.q: Quarter to 6 is how many minutes before 6 o’clock?
items.e: Quarter to 6 is a quarter of an hour before 6 o’clock. That is 15 minutes. Count in 5s back from the 12 to the 9: 5, 10, 15.

The long hand points to the 9: a quarter of an hour before the 12. The short hand is nearly at the 5, but not there yet. It is quarter to 5. (Not quarter to 4: the short hand has passed the 4, so the next hour is 5.)

items.q: At quarter to 4, where is the short hand?
items.e: Quarter to 4 is before 4 o’clock. The short hand is nearly at the 4, but not there yet. It is between 3 and 4.
The long hand points to the 3: a quarter of the way round. The short hand is just past the 6. It is quarter past 6. (Quarter to is when the long hand is on the 9.)
The long hand points to the 3: a quarter of the way round. The short hand is just past the 7. So clock C shows quarter past 7. (Clock A shows quarter to 8. Clock D has the hands swapped.)

The long hand points to the 9: a quarter of an hour before the 12. The short hand is nearly at the 2, but not there yet. It is quarter to 2. (Not quarter to 1: the short hand has passed the 1, so the next hour is 2.)

items.q: How many minutes are in a quarter of an hour?
items.e: 1 hour is 60 minutes. A quarter of 60 is 15. The long hand goes from the 12 to the 3: 5, 10, 15.
The long hand points to the 12. The short hand points to the 5. It is 5 o’clock. On a digital clock that is 5:00. (Not 5:12: the long hand on the 12 means 0 minutes.)
Quarter past 3 is 15 minutes after 3 o’clock: 3:15. (Not 3:03: the long hand on the 3 means 15 minutes.)

The long hand points to the 6: half way round. The short hand is half way between 10 and 11, so the hour is still 10. It is half past 10. On a digital clock that is 10:30. (Not 10:06: the long hand on the 6 means 30 minutes.)
Quarter to 4 is 15 minutes before 4 o’clock. It is still the 3 o’clock hour: 45 minutes past 3. That is 3:45. (4:45 is quarter to 5, and 4:15 is quarter past 4.)

The long hand points to the 3: a quarter of the way round. The short hand is just past the 7. It is quarter past 7. On a digital clock that is 7:15. (Not 7:03: the long hand on the 3 means 15 minutes.)
Half past 9 is 30 minutes after 9 o’clock: 9:30. (10:30 is half past 10.)

The long hand points to the 9: a quarter of an hour before the 12. The short hand is nearly at the 2, but not there yet. It is quarter to 2. On a digital clock that is 1:45. (Not 2:45: quarter to 2 is still in the 1 o’clock hour.)
11 o’clock is 11 hours and 0 minutes: 11:00.

The long hand points to the 6: half way round. The short hand is half way between 2 and 3, so the hour is still 2. It is half past 2. On a digital clock that is 2:30. (Not 2:06: the long hand on the 6 means 30 minutes.)

items.q: What time is this?
items.e: The hour is 2. 15 minutes is a quarter of an hour, so it is quarter past 2.

items.q: At 4:30, where does the long hand point?
items.e: At half past, the long hand is half of the way around the clock. It points to the 6.

items.q: At 10:30, where does the long hand point?
items.e: At half past, the long hand is half of the way around the clock. It points to the 6.

items.q: At 1:30, where does the long hand point?
items.e: At half past, the long hand is half of the way around the clock. It points to the 6.

items.q: At 5:00, where does the long hand point?
items.e: At 5 o'clock the long hand points to the 12. The short hand points to the 5.

items.q: At 9:00, where does the long hand point?
items.e: At 9 o'clock the long hand points to the 12. The short hand points to the 9.

items.q: At 2:00, where does the long hand point?
items.e: At 2 o'clock the long hand points to the 12. The short hand points to the 2.

items.q: At 3:30, where is the short hand?
items.e: The short hand moves slowly. In half an hour it goes halfway to the next number. At 3:30 it is halfway between 3 and 4.

items.q: At 8:30, where is the short hand?
items.e: The short hand moves slowly. In half an hour it goes halfway to the next number. At 8:30 it is halfway between 8 and 9.

items.q: At 11:30, where is the short hand?
items.e: The short hand moves slowly. In half an hour it goes halfway to the next number. At 11:30 it is halfway between 11 and 12.

items.q: At 6:00, where is the short hand?
items.e: At 6 o'clock the short hand points right on the 6.
The long hand points to the 12. The short hand points to the 9. School starts at 9 o’clock.
The long hand points to the 6: half way round. The short hand is half way between 7 and 8, so the hour is still 7. She eats breakfast at half past 7.
The long hand points to the 9: a quarter of an hour before the 12. The short hand is nearly at the 11, but not there yet. So recess is at quarter to 11 (10:45).
The long hand points to the 12. The short hand points to the 3. School finishes at 3 o’clock.

items.q: Lunch is at half past 12. Which digital time is that?
items.e: Half past 12 is 30 minutes after 12 o’clock: 12:30. (1:30 is half past 1.)
The long hand points to the 9: a quarter of an hour before the 12. The short hand is nearly at the 7, but not there yet. He has dinner at quarter to 7 (6:45).

items.q: Ana goes to bed at quarter past 8. Where does the long hand point?
items.e: At quarter past, the long hand points to the 3. The short hand is just past the 8.

items.q: The school bus comes at quarter past 8. Which digital time is that?
items.e: Quarter past 8 is 15 minutes after 8 o’clock: 8:15. (8:45 is quarter to 9.)

items.q: Nico’s football game starts at quarter to 4. Which digital time is that?
items.e: Quarter to 4 is 15 minutes before 4 o’clock. It is still the 3 o’clock hour: 3:45. (4:45 is quarter to 5.)
The clock shows 2 o’clock. 1 hour later the short hand moves on to the next number. Sport ends at 3 o’clock. (1 o’clock is 1 hour before.)
The short hand points to the 7. The long hand points to the 12. It is 7 o'clock: 7:00.
The long hand points to the 6. That is half of the way around, 30 minutes. The short hand is halfway between 7 and 8. It has not reached the 8 yet, so the hour is 7. It is 7:30, half past 7.
The short hand points to the 8. The long hand points to the 12. It is 8 o'clock: 8:00.
The long hand points to the 6. That is half of the way around, 30 minutes. The short hand is halfway between 11 and 12. It has not reached the 12 yet, so the hour is 11. It is 11:30, half past 11.
The long hand points to the 6. That is half of the way around, 30 minutes. The short hand is halfway between 3 and 4. It has not reached the 4 yet, so the hour is 3. It is 3:30, half past 3.
The long hand points to the 6. That is half of the way around, 30 minutes. The short hand is halfway between 8 and 9. It has not reached the 9 yet, so the hour is 8. It is 8:30, half past 8.

items.q: Francis eats breakfast. When could it be?
items.e: We eat breakfast in the morning, before school: 7:00 in the morning.

items.q: School starts. When could it be?
items.e: School starts in the morning: 8:30 in the morning. At night we are asleep.

items.q: Miguel eats dinner with his family. When could it be?
items.e: Dinner is in the evening: 6:00 in the evening. 6:00 in the morning is time for breakfast.

items.q: Camille goes to bed. When could it be?
items.e: We go to bed at night: 8:00 at night. 8:00 in the morning is time for school.
